items.title: Morning Briefing: Oct. 24, 2026
items.excerpt: Here's a rundown of all the news you need to start Saturday, including Jordan declaring three days of mourning after a deadly church attack that killed at least seven people, a US-brokered temporary ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky, and a Russia-Ukraine prisoner swap of 270 servicemen. ## TOP STORIES ... Public Security Directorate spokesman Amer Sartawi described the shooting as a "criminal incident" and said security forces are pursuing the perpetrators. - US first lady announces Oleshky ceasefire between Russia, Ukraine US first lady Melania Trump announced an agreement between Russia and Ukraine to establish a temporary ceasefire in the southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky, intended to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and the evacuation of civilians who wish to leave, with the White House saying the truce is scheduled to begin on Oct. 29. "The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster," she said, adding that the city's remaining population is primarily elderly residents in ... Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said military officials are working to coordinate the ceasefire and that "those who wish to leave the town will be able to do so," adding that the operation requires extensive and complex preparations and that the evacuation is expected to take at least several days. - Russia, Ukraine swap 270 servicemen each in latest prisoner exchange Russian said Moscow and Kyiv swapped 270 servicemen each in the latest prisoner exchange between the two countries, with the returned Russian servicemen currently in neighboring Belarus. The Defense Ministry added that the service members will return to Russia after receiving necessary psychological and medical assistance and will be transported to medical facilities for further treatment and rehabilitation. ... - Israeli forces shot and killed two Palestinians in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron following allegations they opened fire at Israeli settlers, wounding five people. - Australia imposed sanctions on two North Korean companies and two financial brokers for their alleged role in funding Pyongyang’s nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs through fraudulent IT employment schemes. - Storm Austen left more than 160,000 households without power in France, as strong winds prompted weather alerts in 23 departments in the northwest. - A cybersecurity incident disrupted online systems in public schools in Richmond, capital of the US state of Virginia, forcing schools to shift to a technology-free learning environment while remaining open. - President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said Türkiye continues efforts to promote peace across regions, highlighting Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchanges and mediation initiatives in Africa. - The Collective Security Treaty Organization may decide on Armenia’s membership status at its summit in Moscow next month, with Secretary General Taalatbek Masadykov saying the country’s withdrawal "could happen" if the issue is raised. - Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Ottawa is seeking Türkiye’s expertise to strengthen its defenses and build joint military capabilities, while rejecting US allegations of Canadian election interference and reaffirming that Canada will never become America’s 51st state. - International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol warned that the global energy crisis could persist into 2027, saying he sees little reason to expect a return to normal next year. - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the "immediate closure" of Hebron and instructed security forces to prepare a "full lockdown" of the occupied West Bank. - Greece’s parliament passed legislation banning children younger than 15 from accessing major social media platforms, with the measure set to take effect on Jan. 1. - Austria expelled four Russian diplomats for activities deemed incompatible with their diplomatic status, with the Foreign Ministry citing findings by security authorities but providing no details. - The Kremlin said the first tanker carrying Russian diesel fuel under a deal with the US has departed for its buyers, with additional shipments expected to continue regularly. - Russia said trilateral peace talks on Ukraine are scheduled for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, with discussions set to focus on security guarantees for Russia and Ukraine after a peace deal. - France will deploy 70,000 police officers and gendarmes ahead of nationwide protests, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez vowing an "extremely firm" response to violence, looting, and attacks on public buildings. - Ebola has spread to an eighth province in the Democratic Republic of Congo, as the UN food agency warns that hunger threatens treatment continuity for patients and 3.5 million people in outbreak-affected areas face crisis-level food insecurity. - The Pentagon released its seventh batch of UFO records, including reports of a fast-moving black triangular object spotted by federal agents near a secure US facility, historical sightings, and documents on alleged paranormal activity. - Canadian high diver Molly Carlson became the first woman to dive from a free-floating iceberg, completing a nearly 15-meter (49-foot) backward dive into freezing North Atlantic waters off Newfoundland and Labrador. - A new Israeli poll showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc losing three seats to 48, trailing the opposition bloc’s projected 54 seats ahead of the Oct. 27 election, with neither side projected to secure a governing majority. - Gold prices fell toward a three-month low as a selloff in technology stocks prompted investors to cover losses elsewhere, while rising oil prices fueled inflation concerns and expectations of higher interest rates. - Greece suspended state funding to its basketball federation and ordered financial audits amid a match-fixing and bribery investigation involving federation President Vangelis Liolios and five others facing judicial proceedings. - Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan warned that a new military attack on Iran would widen regional conflict, saying military intervention was “by no means a solution” amid concerns about renewed US-Israeli strikes. - Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was hospitalized after collapsing while watching the club’s reserve team train, with the 40-year-old Belgian set to undergo medical examinations as his coaching staff takes charge until further notice. - Yemen said it neutralized 620 Houthi fighters and destroyed or damaged 190 military vehicles and weapons systems in 1,392 operations under "Operation Dawn of Yemen" in 24 hours. - US President Donald Trump warned of possible renewed military action against Iran if Tehran rejects negotiations, while saying Washington would "take care of Cuba" after dealing with Iran. - The International Atomic Energy Agency said it is ready to verify Iran’s nuclear activities, with chief Rafael Grossi urging a diplomatic agreement and saying most technical preparations needed for adequate verification have been completed. - The Trump administration removed several Canadian products from its 50% tariff list, with changes taking effect Oct. 30 ahead of hard-fought US midterm elections. ## SPORTS

items.title: Economy - Axios
items.excerpt: One of the final snapshots of how Americans feel about the economy before voters head to the polls in the midterm elections shows a nation still deeply frustrated by the cost of living. By the numbers: The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index registered 48 in October, virtually unchanged from September's 48.1 and revised higher from a preliminary reading of 46.3. - That initial estimate was the second-lowest in the survey's history, behind the all-time low hit in May. - Even after the upward revision, sentiment remains 10% below its level this time last year. ... Zoom in: Beneath the flat headline reading, consumers grew more pessimistic about current economic conditions, with that index falling more than 4 points to 46.7. - Buying conditions for durable goods plunged 18% amid high prices and rising borrowing costs — accounting for the entire decline in consumers' assessment of current economic conditions. - "Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," Joanne Hsu, director of the survey, said in the release. - But consumers' outlook for the future improved, with the expectations sub-index rising 2.5 points to 48.8.

items.title: US business activity cools in October; strong demand fueling price pressures By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US business activity slowed modestly in October, though robust demand allowed companies to raise prices for goods and services, a sign that inflation could increase further and remain persistently high in the coming months. S&P Global said on Friday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, slipped to 57.6 this month from a five-year high reading of 58.4 in September. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. Strength in manufacturing was offset by a slight pullback in the vast services sector. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid footing following what is expected to have been a strong performance in the July-September quarter. Economists expect the government’s advance gross domestic product report next week to show the economy growing at around a 3.0% annualized rate last quarter, mainly driven by consumer spending and business investment in AI. ... Consumer and producer prices increased strongly in September, the government reported this month, raising concerns that inflation was fanning out across the economy. The Federal Reserve in September raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range.

items.excerpt: - AP - Oct 24, 2026 - Oct 24, 2026 Updated 2 hrs ago - 0 ... Trump at South Florida rally revives the idea of military intervention in Cuba after Iran FORT MYERS, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump on Friday told a rally for candidates in South Florida that U.S. warships returning from the Middle East could stop over in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war, his latest suggestion of taking an interventionist approach to the nearby country. Trump first floated this idea earlier this year, but has not mentioned it in recent months. But he revived it in response to a shouted question from the crowd about the island nation. He was campaigning just days ahead of midterm elections in which voters have expressed concern about the impact the U.S. war on Iran has had on prices of goods from gas to groceries. “We’ll do a little stopover,” Trump said. “Actually, what we’re going to do with Cuba is, we’re going to come back from Iran. Those beautiful ships will pass Cuba. We’ll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They’ll raise up their hands. And then we’re going to send (Secretary of State) Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal.” Both Rubio and Trump have been bullish on action in Cuba, with Trump previously suggesting the country would "be next” in terms of intervention abroad, following the winding down of the Iran war he has long forecast but which has not yet happened. ... In May, he and Rubio raised the specter of U.S. military intervention in Cuba, a renewed threat that took on greater weight after the administration announced criminal charges against the island’s former leader, Raúl Castro. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that previous U.S. presidents had considered intervening in Cuba for decades but that “it looks like I’ll be the one that does it.” Trump says he ordered the Justice Department's lawsuit over Alaska's US Senate race President Donald Trump on Friday said he told his administration to file its lawsuit to block certification of the U.S. Senate race in Alaska if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, kicking off what many fear could become a lengthy battle between the government and states over certifying an election where the president's party is struggling. “I'm the one that said do it,” Trump told reporters as he landed for a campaign rally in Florida. The lawsuit, filed late Thursday, centers on one of the president's longstanding complaints in the Senate race — the presence of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan, who Republicans fear could siphon away votes from the incumbent in what's likely to be a photo-finish contest with Democrat Mary Peltola, the state's former congresswoman. The second Sullivan, who is Daniel J. Sullivan from the tiny fishing community of Petersburg, has said he decided to run on his own, but Republicans have contended he is a Democratic plant to siphon votes away from their candidate. The lawsuit by the Republican president's Department of Justice in federal court in Alaska demands that the state be blocked from certifying a Peltola win if Daniel J. Sullivan remains on the ballot. “The United States accordingly brings this lawsuit to protect the integrity of the 2026 Senate election in Alaska,” the lawsuit says. Ukraine and Russia eye new peace talks — and Melania Trump's mission — but steep obstacles remain KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukraine and Russia have signaled their willingness to resume U.S.-brokered peace talks and are backing a humanitarian mission led by First Lady Melania Trump. But deep disagreements over territory and security guarantees that re-emerged this week underscore obstacles to ending the war. The new diplomatic push comes after more than 4½ years of fighting, bringing with it a surprise announcement on Friday: Kyiv and Moscow have agreed to a local ceasefire to allow aid next week into a stranded town in Ukraine's southern war-divided region of Kherson, following secret consultations between Melania Trump and civilian negotiators from Russia and Ukraine. While the initiative raised hopes of similar humanitarian missions in the future, there were few indications that any of the key positions have shifted. Russia continues to demand Ukrainian territory it does not fully control, while Kyiv insists any agreement must include ironclad guarantees against another invasion. Within hours of Russian President Vladimir Putin saying he agreed “in principle” to restart talks, Russia launched a deadly barrage of ballistic missiles and drones on Kyiv. Moscow on the same day said it had destroyed more than 800 Ukrainian drones heading toward its cities. ... Here’s a look at where the two countries stand as potential negotiations loom. U.S. presidential envoy Steve Witkoff secured the latest commitment to talks after shuttling between Oslo, Norway, and St. Petersburg, Russia, this week to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Putin. A new round of negotiations would be the fourth brokered by the Trump administration, following the most recent round in Geneva in February. A Kremlin spokesman said that the next round of talks is likely to be held in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, around mid-November. Western governments backing the peace initiative are seeking a new formula to break the impasse while acknowledging that territorial and security questions remain unresolved. 2 ex-FBI officials charged with lying about involvement in investigation into Hunter Biden's laptop WASHINGTON (AP) — Two former FBI officials were charged Friday with lying to Congress about their involvement in investigating Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election, the latest in a series of splashy and politically charged actions the Justice Department has undertaken ahead of next month's midterm contests. Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former leaders of a since-disbanded task force set up to counter foreign election interference, appeared in federal court in Washington, where their lawyers pressed for a speedy hearing to contest allegations their clients lied to lawmakers by saying that they did not participate in FBI investigations of Biden. The prosecution, a rare Department of Justice criminal case against a former employee, revisits a tangled and peculiar saga that roiled the final weeks of the 2020 race. It also comes amid a broader, backward-looking effort by FBI Director Kash Patel, who before taking over the nation’s premier law enforcement agency was a harsh critic of it, to scrutinize high-profile episodes from the bureau’s recent past that for years have animated President Donald Trump’s conservative base. ... Obama is set to campaign with Democrats in Ohio and Michigan as he ramps up midterm efforts Barack Obama will campaign Saturday with Democratic candidates for the U.S. Senate in Ohio and Michigan, both highly competitive states that will help determine control of the chamber, as the former president ramps up his involvement in the midterm elections. Obama's first event is in Cleveland with former three-term Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown, who is looking to unseat Republican Sen. Jon Husted. Amy Acton, a Democrat running for governor against Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, will also appear at the rally. items.title: Jay-Z Brings Out Blue Ivy, DJ Khaled at Los Angeles' SoFi Stadium
items.excerpt: “Can I take you to my home for a second?” asked Jay-Z as he led into “Empire State of Mind” during the first of two headlining shows at Inglewood, California’s SoFi Stadium. Thus, he did, as he’d been doing for the past hour-and-a-half, bringing Brooklyn to Los Angeles as he traced the corners of his vast discography, the backbone of a career that stretches 30 years with countless ... As he’s consistently shown, Jay was in mint condition as he ran through hit after hit after hit at SoFi across a two-hour set, toggling the setlist of previous shows while keeping the focus centered on the electricity between himself, the audience and his band. Fans have, of course, come to expect high-wattage surprise stars: At his Yankee Stadium shows, he coronated the 25th and 30th anniversaries of “The Blueprint” and “Reasonable Doubt,” respectively, with cameos from his wife Beyoncé, Rihanna, Eminem and his daughter Blue Ivy Carter, to name just a few. His SoFi show, meanwhile, felt pared-down with purpose. There were few guest stars throughout the night, with Blue Ivy playing the keys on “The Story of OJ” and “Dead Presidents,” a shift from when she tickled the ivories on “Feelin’ It” at Yankee Stadium. Scarface came out for “This Can’t Be Life” as well as his own classic “Mind Playing Tricks on Me.” John Legend and DJ Khaled emerged for the night’s closer, “God Did,” a song that originally also featured Fridayy, Lil Wayne and Rick Ross.
